Its range is wide, usually covering four or five octaves: the top is sharp and exciting, the middle mild and clear, the low end deep and resonant. Compared with the thin, piercing traditional xylophone, the xylorimba has a rounder, fuller tone because of the way its bars are made; compared with the soft warmth of the marimba it is sharper and brighter. The instrument uses wooden bars with resonators, so the sound projects well and sustains. The top sounds like glittering light, while the low end has a deep resonance; overall the sound has both carrying power and depth of resonance, and suits complex melodic lines and rich layers of timbre.

Resonator tubes sit under the bars, usually of bamboo or wood, to increase volume and resonance. The frame is of wood or metal, which keeps the instrument stable. It is played with soft mallets whose heads are usually covered in rubber or felt, which adjusts the brightness. The whole structure combines wood and metal to get the best sound.

The xylorimba is an idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 111.21, a tuned percussion instrument. It is built as a row of wooden bars arranged like a piano keyboard, its range covering the low end of the marimba up to the top of the xylophone, and it has resonators. It is not a hybrid of xylophone and marimba, though the name easily misleads. It was popular in vaudeville theatres in the 1920s and 1930s; composers such as Berg, Boulez and Messiaen used it in their works, and Boulez wrote for two five-octave xylorimbas in Pli selon pli.
木琴馬林巴見於二十世紀管弦樂、室內樂、歌劇與打擊樂合奏，也曾用於雜耍歌舞劇場。皮: The xylorimba appears in twentieth-century orchestral music, chamber music, opera and percussion ensembles, and was also used in vaudeville. Pierre Boulez wrote two five-octave xylorimbas for soprano and orchestra in Pli selon pli; Olivier Messiaen used it alongside piano, horn, glockenspiel and orchestra in Des Canyons aux étoiles.... There are also line-ups with soprano, baritone, mixed chorus, and cor anglais, flute, harp and percussion ensemble.
木琴馬林巴起源於非洲，為馬林巴樂器家族的一員。馬林巴最初在坦桑尼亞和莫桑比克等地: The xylorimba originated in Africa and is a member of the marimba family. The marimba first developed in places such as Tanzania and Mozambique and later spread to Central America, especially Guatemala and Mexico, where it evolved into many forms. The xylorimba, a hybrid percussion instrument, arose from the demand for a wider range.
隨著現代作曲技術的發展，二十世紀作曲家如阿爾班·貝爾格、皮埃爾·布列茲和奧利維埃: As modern compositional technique developed, twentieth-century composers such as Alban Berg, Pierre Boulez and Olivier Messiaen asked in their works for percussion instruments with a wider range. Despite the confusing name, many composers in fact needed only the standard four-octave xylophone, but the vagueness of the name persisted widely. The xylorimba gradually won recognition in Western classical and contemporary music and became one of the important percussion instruments of the symphony orchestra and the chamber ensemble.
